Principle 25: My country
Our country’s history began about 5,000 years ago.
The first country’s ancient name was Gojoson.
After it fell, the Korean peninsula was divided into three Kingdoms.
Later these three kingdoms united as a single nation called
the Shilla Kingdom.
After Shilla fell, many other countries tried to control Korea.
For a while, Korea was ruled by Japan.
Our country was liberated from Japan in 1945.
The Korean Civil War in 1950 divided the Korean peninsula into
North and South Korea.
After the war, the country developed very quickly.
We hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1988
and the World Cup in 2002.
I am proud of what my country has accomplished during its long history.
My country has many traditional holidays.
There are Lunar New Year’s, Independence Day,
Buddha’s Birthday, Chu-seok and many more.
Lunar New Year’s is the first big holiday celebrated of the year.
Perhaps the biggest national holiday of the year is Chu-seok
or what is also referred to as Korean Thanksgiving Day.
Our culture is different from other cultures.
For example, our clothes, housing, names,
and language are not like that of any other country.
I would like to explain about our traditional food.
Traditional Korean meals include boiled rice, soup, fish or meat,
several vegetable side dishes, and, one or more kinds of kimchi.
My favorite food is bulgogi.
Bulgogi is the most popular Korean meat dish.
I am used to eating these delicious foods every day.
Our country has many places to visit such as Gyeong-ju,
Bulguk-Temple, Mt. Halla and the Korea Folk Village.
The most historical attraction in Korea is the city of Gyeong-ju.
Gyeong-ju was the ancient capital of the Shilla Kingdom.
The Shilla Kingdom was at its most powerful during the 8th century.
Many people refer to Gyeong-ju as a museum without walls
because it contains many old remains of the Shilla Dynasty.
Another popular place to visit is Mt. Halla on the island of Jeju.
It is located near the center of the island, and it is South Korea’s
tallest mountain, standing at almost 2,000 meters tall.
I would like to visit these marvelousplaces someday.
